name: California
description:
**California** is the powerhouse of American wine, stretching down the western coast of the United States and responsible for the vast majority of the country's production.

**Wines & grapes** — Just about every style is made here, but the signatures are ripe, generous Cabernet Sauvignon (especially from Napa Valley), buttery or crisp Chardonnay, spicy Zinfandel, and increasingly refined Pinot Noir from cooler coastal pockets like Sonoma and the Central Coast.

**Character** — A warm, sunny climate delivers full-bodied, fruit-forward wines with plenty of ripeness and often a polished, oak-influenced style, though fog and ocean breezes let cooler sites hold onto freshness. **Good to know** — Napa Valley is the prestige address, but California spans dozens of climates, from the foggy coast to the hot Central Valley.

name: Burgundy
description:
**Burgundy** (Bourgogne) is a historic region in eastern France, revered as the spiritual home of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay and famous for its intense focus on individual vineyard sites.

**Wines & grapes** — Almost everything is red Pinot Noir or white Chardonnay, made as single-variety wines. The region also gives us Chablis (steely Chardonnay in the north) and Beaujolais to the south, where the Gamay grape rules.

**Character** — A cool continental climate and limestone-rich soils produce wines of finesse, transparency, and remarkable expression of place, where neighbouring plots can taste distinctly different. **Good to know** — Burgundy's classification runs from regional wines up through Village, Premier Cru, and the rare, coveted Grand Cru vineyards.

name: Champagne
description:
**Champagne** is the cool northern French region that gave its name to the world's most celebrated sparkling wine, made by a second fermentation in the bottle.

**Wines & grapes** — Primarily sparkling wines built from three grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, and Pinot Meunier. Styles range from non-vintage blends to vintage cuvées, Blanc de Blancs (all Chardonnay), Blanc de Noirs, and rosé.

**Character** — The chilly climate and chalky soils keep grapes high in acidity, which is the backbone of Champagne's freshness, fine bubbles, and ageworthiness, while lees ageing adds toasty, biscuity depth. **Good to know** — Only sparkling wine from this region may legally be called Champagne; similar wines made elsewhere go by other names.

name: Bordeaux
description:
**Bordeaux** is a large, historically influential wine region in southwestern France centred on the Gironde estuary, famous above all for its structured, ageworthy red blends.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds dominate, built mainly from Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot (with Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot, and Malbec in support). It also makes dry whites from Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon, plus the sweet, botrytised wines of Sauternes.

**Character** — The Left Bank (gravel soils) favours firm, Cabernet-led wines; the Right Bank (clay and limestone) leans on plush, Merlot-led ones. **Good to know** — The 1855 Classification ranked the top Médoc châteaux into five growths, a hierarchy still referenced today.

name: Tuscany
description:
**Tuscany** (Toscana) is one of Italy's most iconic wine regions, set in the rolling hills of the country's centre and inseparable from the Sangiovese grape.

**Wines & grapes** — Sangiovese is the star, driving Chianti, Brunello di Montalcino, and Vino Nobile di Montepulciano. The region also gave rise to the so-called Super Tuscans, bold reds often blending Sangiovese with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, alongside the sweet Vin Santo.

**Character** — A warm Mediterranean climate and varied hillside soils give reds marked by bright cherry fruit, savoury herbs, firm tannins, and lively acidity that suits the table. **Good to know** — Brunello di Montalcino must be made from 100% Sangiovese and given long ageing before release.

name: Piedmont
description:
**Piedmont** (Piemonte) sits in the northwest of Italy, tucked against the Alps, and is prized for some of the country's most serious and long-lived red wines.

**Wines & grapes** — The noble Nebbiolo grape makes the powerful, perfumed reds of Barolo and Barbaresco. Everyday drinking comes from Barbera and Dolcetto, while Moscato d'Asti and sparkling Asti offer sweet, low-alcohol whites.

**Character** — A continental climate with autumn fog (nebbia, which lends Nebbiolo its name) yields wines high in tannin and acidity, with signature aromas of rose, tar, cherry, and dried herbs that unfold with age. **Good to know** — Barolo and Barbaresco are often called the "king and queen" of Italian wine.

name: Rhône Valley
description:
**Rhône Valley** (Vallée du Rhône) follows the Rhône river through southeastern France and splits into two distinct halves with very different personalities.

**Wines & grapes** — The steep northern Rhône makes Syrah-based reds (Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage) and whites from Viognier, Marsanne, and Roussanne. The broader, warmer south favours Grenache-led blends, most famously Châteauneuf-du-Pape, which can draw on more than a dozen permitted grapes.

**Character** — Northern wines are focused and peppery; southern wines are warm, generous, and herb-scented, shaped by the drying Mistral wind and stony soils. **Good to know** — The rounded galets (large pebbles) of Châteauneuf-du-Pape store daytime heat and release it at night.

name: Central Otago
description:
**Central Otago** lies in the mountainous interior of New Zealand's South Island and is one of the world's southernmost wine regions, best known for its Pinot Noir.

**Wines & grapes** — Pinot Noir is the flagship, with smaller amounts of Pinot Gris, Riesling, Chardonnay, and aromatic whites.

**Character** — Unusually for New Zealand, the climate is semi-continental rather than maritime, with hot days, cold nights, and dry autumns. This gives Pinot Noir deep colour, ripe dark-cherry fruit, and a vivid, fresh energy. **Good to know** — The dramatic landscape of lakes and mountains makes it one of the most scenic wine regions anywhere.

name: South Australia
description:
**South Australia** is the engine room of Australian wine, producing a large share of the nation's output and home to many of its most famous names.

**Wines & grapes** — Shiraz is the calling card, especially the rich, powerful reds of the Barossa Valley and McLaren Vale. The region also excels with Cabernet Sauvignon from Coonawarra, Riesling from the cool Clare and Eden Valleys, and Chardonnay from the Adelaide Hills.

**Character** — Climates range from hot, dry inland valleys to cooler elevated sites, but the reds are typically full-bodied, ripe, and generous with dark fruit and spice. **Good to know** — The Barossa is home to some of the oldest continuously producing Shiraz vines on earth, having escaped the phylloxera louse.

name: Hawke's Bay
description:
**Hawke's Bay** is a warm coastal region on the east side of New Zealand's North Island and one of the country's oldest and most versatile wine areas.

**Wines & grapes** — Best known for Bordeaux-style reds from Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, plus Syrah and full-bodied Chardonnay. The gravelly Gimblett Gravels sub-zone is especially prized for reds.

**Character** — A relatively sunny, sheltered climate lets red grapes ripen fully, giving structured, savoury wines with good depth, while the Chardonnays combine ripeness with freshness. **Good to know** — Hawke's Bay offers a warmer counterpoint to the cooler, Sauvignon-Blanc-dominated Marlborough region.

name: Pfalz
description:
**Pfalz** (the Palatinate) is a sunny wine region in southwestern Germany, running along the eastern edge of the Haardt hills as a northern continuation of France's Alsace.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling is the leading grape, made in styles from bone-dry to sweet, alongside a strong showing of Pinot varieties: Pinot Gris (Grauburgunder), Pinot Blanc (Weissburgunder), and Pinot Noir (Spätburgunder).

**Character** — One of Germany's warmest, driest regions, the Pfalz ripens grapes readily, producing Rieslings that are riper, rounder, and often drier than those of the cooler Mosel. **Good to know** — Its mild climate even allows figs and almonds to flourish among the vines.

name: Veneto
description:
**Veneto** is a prolific region in northeastern Italy, running from Lake Garda toward Venice, and one of the country's largest producers by volume.

**Wines & grapes** — It is famous for Prosecco (sparkling wine from the Glera grape), the reds of Valpolicella and the rich, dried-grape Amarone (from Corvina and friends), and crisp whites like Soave, made from Garganega.

**Character** — A range of climates from alpine foothills to the warm plains supports everything from light, fresh everyday wines to concentrated, powerful reds. **Good to know** — Amarone is made by drying the grapes for months before pressing, a process called appassimento that concentrates sugar and flavour.

name: Napa Valley
description:
**Napa Valley** is a compact, sun-warmed valley in northern California, an hour or so above San Francisco, and it is the name that turned American wine into a serious global player.

**Wines & grapes** — Cabernet Sauvignon is king here, producing rich, structured reds that are the region's calling card, often bottled as single-varietal wines or Bordeaux-style blends with Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Chardonnay is the leading white, and you will also find Sauvignon Blanc, Zinfandel, and Merlot.

**Character** — The valley's warm days and cool, fog-influenced nights let grapes ripen fully while keeping their freshness, giving wines that are ripe, generous, and built to age. Distinct sub-areas such as Rutherford, Oakville, Stags Leap, and the mountain slopes each lend their own signature. **Good to know** — Napa reds are among the most collectible and priciest wines made outside Europe.

name: Mosel
description:
**Mosel** follows the twisting Mosel River in western Germany, near the borders with Luxembourg and France, and is one of the world's great homes for Riesling.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling dominates overwhelmingly, made in a spectrum from bone-dry (trocken) to lusciously sweet late-harvest bottlings such as Spätlese, Auslese, and the rare Trockenbeerenauslese. Smaller amounts of Müller-Thurgau and Elbling are also grown.

**Character** — The vines cling to breathtakingly steep slopes of blue and grey slate that soak up warmth and reflect it back, helping grapes ripen in this cool, northerly climate. The results are famously light in alcohol, vivid with citrus and orchard fruit, and threaded with a bright, mineral acidity. **Good to know** — The finest sites, like the Bernkasteler Doctor and Wehlener Sonnenuhr, are among Germany's most revered vineyards.

name: Sicily
description:
**Sicily** is the large Mediterranean island off the toe of Italy, and one of the country's most exciting and fast-improving wine regions.

**Wines & grapes** — Nero d'Avola is the signature red grape, giving warm, full-bodied wines, while the volcanic slopes of Mount Etna produce more delicate, age-worthy reds from Nerello Mascalese and crisp whites from Carricante. Native whites like Grillo, Catarratto, and Inzolia are widely planted, and the island is also the source of the fortified dessert wine Marsala.

**Character** — Abundant sunshine and sea breezes shape ripe, sun-soaked wines, but the high-altitude, mineral-rich volcanic soils of Etna have earned a cult following for their freshness and finesse. **Good to know** — Sicily has shifted from bulk production toward quality, and Etna in particular is now spoken of alongside the world's great cool-climate reds.

name: Loire Valley
description:
**Loire Valley** stretches along France's longest river, running west from the centre of the country toward the Atlantic coast, and is prized above all for elegant, food-friendly whites.

**Wines & grapes** — It is a patchwork of styles: crisp Sauvignon Blanc from Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé, versatile Chenin Blanc from Vouvray and Savennières (dry, sweet, and sparkling), light Cabernet Franc reds from Chinon and Bourgueil, and tangy Muscadet made from Melon de Bourgogne near the sea.

**Character** — This is one of France's cooler regions, so freshness and bright acidity define the wines, along with a pronounced sense of the varied soils, from flinty limestone to schist. **Good to know** — The valley's sparkling Crémant de Loire and its long-lived sweet Chenins are among France's best-value classics.

name: Rheinhessen
description:
**Rheinhessen** sits in a gentle, rolling stretch of land within a bend of the Rhine in western Germany, and is the country's largest wine region by area.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling is the flagship and produces the most distinguished wines, though Müller-Thurgau, Silvaner, and a growing amount of red Dornfelder and Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir) are also important. Both dry and off-dry styles are common.

**Character** — Once known mainly for large volumes of soft, simple wine, Rheinhessen has been reinvented by a wave of quality-focused growers, especially along the steep slopes of the Rheinterrasse near Nierstein and Nackenheim. There the reddish slate and sandstone soils give Rieslings real depth and mineral drive. **Good to know** — Its younger generation of winemakers has made it one of Germany's most dynamic regions.

name: Languedoc-Roussillon
description:
**Languedoc-Roussillon** is a vast sweep of vineyards along France's southern Mediterranean coast, running from the Rhône toward the Spanish border, and is one of the largest wine-producing areas in the world.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds and rosés dominate, built from the classic southern French grapes Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre, and Carignan, often blended together. Whites come from Picpoul, Grenache Blanc, and others, and the region also makes distinctive fortified sweet wines (vins doux naturels) such as Banyuls and Muscat.

**Character** — A sunny, dry Mediterranean climate yields warm, herby, generous wines carrying the scent of the local wild scrubland known as garrigue. **Good to know** — Long a source of everyday bulk wine, it now offers some of France's best value alongside ambitious appellations like Corbières, Minervois, and Pic Saint-Loup.

name: Rioja
description:
**Rioja** is Spain's most famous wine region, set inland in the north along the Ebro River, and is renowned for its supple, oak-aged red wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Tempranillo is the heart of Rioja's reds, usually blended with Garnacha (Grenache) and smaller amounts of Graciano and Mazuelo. Traditional white Rioja is made mainly from Viura, and both reds and whites can spend long periods maturing in barrel.

**Character** — Wines are classified by ageing: Crianza, Reserva, and Gran Reserva mark increasing time in oak and bottle, with the classic style showing savoury, vanilla-and-leather notes from American oak alongside red fruit. **Good to know** — Rioja splits into three zones, Rioja Alta, Rioja Alavesa, and Rioja Oriental, and ranges from crowd-pleasing everyday bottles to profound, decades-lived Gran Reservas.

name: Mendoza
description:
**Mendoza** lies in the arid foothills of the Andes in western Argentina and is by far the country's most important wine region, responsible for the majority of its production.

**Wines & grapes** — Malbec is the signature grape, producing deeply coloured, plush, dark-fruited reds that made Argentina's international name. Cabernet Sauvignon, Bonarda, and Syrah are also widely grown, along with the aromatic white Torrontés.

**Character** — Vineyards sit at high altitude, sometimes above 1,000 metres, where intense sunlight and cool nights give ripe fruit with lively acidity and firm colour. The desert climate relies on meltwater irrigation channelled down from the snowcapped Andes. **Good to know** — Higher, cooler sub-zones like the Uco Valley have pushed Mendoza's Malbec toward greater freshness and elegance.

name: Stellenbosch
description:
**Stellenbosch** is South Africa's best-known fine-wine district, set among granite hills just inland from Cape Town, and is the historic centre of the country's quality wine trade.

**Wines & grapes** — It is especially celebrated for structured reds, above all Cabernet Sauvignon and Bordeaux-style blends, along with Syrah/Shiraz, Pinotage (South Africa's own crossing), and characterful whites from Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon Blanc.

**Character** — A warm but sea-cooled Mediterranean climate, combined with varied mountain slopes and diverse soils, allows a wide range of styles, with the reds tending toward ripe fruit and firm structure. **Good to know** — Stellenbosch is also home to South Africa's leading wine university and research, and many of the Cape's most acclaimed estates.

name: Western Cape
description:
**Western Cape** is the broad South African province that contains almost all of the country's vineyards, sweeping inland and along the coast from Cape Town.

**Wines & grapes** — As an umbrella region it spans nearly every style the country makes: Chenin Blanc (its most-planted grape) and Sauvignon Blanc among the whites, and Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah/Shiraz, and the local Pinotage among the reds.

**Character** — The climate is largely Mediterranean, moderated by the cold Benguela Current off the Atlantic coast and by the cooling Cape Doctor wind, with ancient, weathered soils underfoot. Because it covers so many districts, from Stellenbosch and Paarl to cooler coastal sites, its wines vary widely. **Good to know** — Wines simply labelled Western Cape are often blends drawn from several districts across the province.

name: Douro
description:
**Douro** runs along the dramatic, terraced valley of the Douro River in northern Portugal and is the birthplace of Port, one of the world's classic fortified wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Alongside sweet, fortified Port in its many styles (Ruby, Tawny, Vintage), the region increasingly makes highly regarded dry reds and whites. Both draw on a palette of native grapes such as Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz (Tempranillo), and Tinta Barroca.

**Character** — Steeply terraced schist slopes bake under a hot, dry continental climate, concentrating the fruit into powerful, dark, structured wines. **Good to know** — One of the oldest demarcated wine regions in the world, the Douro's spectacular landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its dry reds now rival its Ports for prestige.

name: Barossa Valley
description:
**Barossa Valley** lies northeast of Adelaide in South Australia and is one of the country's most iconic wine regions, famous for bold, full-bodied reds.

**Wines & grapes** — Shiraz is the star, giving rich, concentrated, dark-fruited wines with real power, and the valley is also known for Grenache, Mourvèdre (often blended GSM-style), and Cabernet Sauvignon. On the cooler high ground of the Eden Valley nearby, Riesling shines.

**Character** — A warm, dry climate produces ripe, generous wines with soft tannins and a signature depth. Barossa is treasured above all for its old vines, some among the oldest continuously producing vineyards on earth, planted by 19th-century German settlers. **Good to know** — Wines from these ancient vines can be extraordinarily concentrated and long-lived.

name: Nahe
description:
**Nahe** — a German wine region in the southwest, named for the Nahe river that winds through it before joining the Rhine near Bingen. It sits between the Mosel and Rheinhessen and is best known for expressive, mineral Riesling.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling is the star, made in styles from bone-dry to lusciously sweet. You will also find Müller-Thurgau, Weissburgunder (Pinot Blanc), Grauburgunder (Pinot Gris) and some Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir).

**Character** — The Nahe is famous for its geological patchwork: within a short distance the soils shift between slate, volcanic rock, quartzite and sandstone. This variety gives the Rieslings a wide range of expression, often combining ripe stone-fruit flavours with firm, stony minerality and bright acidity.

**Good to know** — It is one of Germany's smaller and often underrated regions, prized by enthusiasts for offering great quality at fair prices.

name: Baden
description:
**Baden** — Germany's southernmost and warmest major wine region, a long, narrow strip running down the southwest of the country, much of it facing the Vosges mountains and Alsace across the Rhine.

**Wines & grapes** — Unusually for Germany, red wine is a real strength here. Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir) leads, alongside the Pinot family of whites — Grauburgunder (Pinot Gris) and Weissburgunder (Pinot Blanc) — plus Riesling, Müller-Thurgau and the local Gutedel (Chasselas) in the far south.

**Character** — The warmer, sunnier climate produces riper, rounder and often fuller-bodied wines than most of Germany. Volcanic soils in areas like the Kaiserstuhl add depth and structure, giving reds real substance and whites a generous, food-friendly weight.

**Good to know** — Baden is the heartland of dry, Burgundian-styled German wine, reflecting its cultural and culinary closeness to neighbouring France.

name: Puglia
description:
**Puglia** — the long region forming the heel of Italy's boot, running down the southeast Adriatic coast. It is one of the country's largest wine producers, historically a source of robust, sun-soaked reds.

**Wines & grapes** — The signatures are Primitivo (genetically the same as Zinfandel) and Negroamaro, both making deep, warm, generous reds; Nero di Troia adds a more structured, tannic style further north around Foggia.

**Character** — A hot, dry Mediterranean climate and flat, fertile plains give wines that are ripe, full-bodied and high in alcohol, with soft tannins and dark fruit, sometimes with a warm, almost baked or spicy edge.

**Good to know** — Once known mainly for bulk wine and blending grapes shipped north, Puglia has increasingly focused on quality, and its Primitivo di Manduria and Salice Salentino bottlings offer great value.

name: Alsace
description:
**Alsace** — a distinctive wine region in northeastern France, tucked between the Vosges mountains and the Rhine along the German border. Its history has shuffled between France and Germany, and this shows in both its grapes and its tall, flute-shaped bottles.

**Wines & grapes** — Alsace is above all a white-wine region, and unusually for France it labels most wines by grape. Riesling and Gewürztraminer are the flagships, joined by Pinot Gris, Muscat and Pinot Blanc, with Pinot Noir the main red. It also makes fine sparkling Crémant d'Alsace.

**Character** — The Vosges shelter the vineyards from rain, making this one of France's driest and sunniest areas. The wines are aromatic and full-flavoured, ranging from bracingly dry to richly sweet late-harvest styles.

**Good to know** — Fifty-one Grand Cru vineyards mark its finest sites.

name: Finger Lakes
description:
**Finger Lakes** — a cool-climate wine region in upstate New York, USA, named for a group of long, narrow glacial lakes. It is the most important wine area on the American East Coast for serious European-style whites.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling is the calling card, made in styles from dry to sweet, alongside Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer and increasingly good Cabernet Franc and Pinot Noir among the reds.

**Character** — The deep lakes act as heat reservoirs, moderating the harsh winters and protecting vines near their shores. The cool growing season yields wines with vibrant acidity, moderate alcohol and pure fruit — Rieslings here often show crisp citrus and orchard fruit with a lively, refreshing edge.

**Good to know** — Its climate is frequently compared to Germany's, and Riesling is what put the region on the international map.

name: Castilla y León
description:
**Castilla y León** — a large region on the high central plateau of northern Spain, spread across the Duero river basin. It holds several of the country's most celebrated appellations.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds built on Tempranillo dominate, going by local names such as Tinto Fino in Ribera del Duero and Tinta de Toro in Toro; both make powerful, age-worthy wines. For whites, the Rueda zone specialises in fresh, aromatic Verdejo.

**Character** — The plateau sits at high altitude with a continental climate: hot days and cold nights, with a big daily temperature swing. This helps the reds keep firm acidity and structure alongside deep, concentrated dark fruit, while the whites stay crisp and lively.

**Good to know** — Ribera del Duero, Toro and Rueda are the headline DOs, but the wider region includes many others such as Bierzo (made from Mencía).

name: Catalonia
description:
**Catalonia** — a region in northeastern Spain centred on Barcelona, stretching from the Mediterranean coast into the mountainous interior. It is one of Spain's most dynamic and varied wine areas.

**Wines & grapes** — It is the home of Cava, Spain's traditional-method sparkling wine, largely made in Penedès from Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada. Priorat and neighbouring Montsant produce concentrated reds from old-vine Garnacha (Grenache) and Cariñena (Carignan), while Penedès also makes a wide range of still whites and reds, including international varieties.

**Character** — Styles span from crisp, fresh sparkling and coastal whites to dense, mineral, powerful reds from the steep slate terraces (llicorella) of Priorat.

**Good to know** — Priorat is one of only two Spanish regions to hold the top DOCa/DOQ status, the same tier as Rioja.

name: Rheingau
description:
**Rheingau** — a compact, historic wine region in Germany where the Rhine briefly turns to flow east-to-west, giving a long stretch of south-facing slopes. Despite its small size it has an outsized reputation.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling rules here, made in dry to nobly sweet styles of real precision and longevity. Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir), particularly around Assmannshausen, is the notable red.

**Character** — The river's east-west bend maximises sun exposure and reflects light and warmth onto the vineyards, while slate and other soils lend the Rieslings their structure. The wines tend to be fuller, firmer and more powerful than those of the Mosel, with pronounced minerality and the capacity to age for decades.

**Good to know** — The Rheingau is a cradle of German wine history: it was here that Schloss Johannisberg helped pioneer late-harvest Spätlese wines.

name: Sonoma County
description:
**Sonoma County** — a large and varied wine region on the coast of Northern California, USA, just west of Napa Valley. It runs from the cool, fog-swept Pacific shore inland to warmer valleys, giving it a huge range of growing conditions.

**Wines & grapes** — Cooler zones like the Russian River Valley and Sonoma Coast excel at Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; warmer inland areas such as Alexander Valley and Dry Creek Valley shine with Cabernet Sauvignon and old-vine Zinfandel.

**Character** — With coastal fog and many small sub-appellations, Sonoma spans everything from bright, elegant cool-climate wines to rich, full-bodied reds. It generally feels a touch more rustic and diverse than its polished Napa neighbour.

**Good to know** — It contains numerous distinct AVAs, so the county name covers many very different wine styles.

name: Marlborough
description:
**Marlborough** — New Zealand's largest and most famous wine region, at the sunny northeastern tip of the South Island. It is the area that made New Zealand a global name in wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Sauvignon Blanc is the overwhelming signature, defining a whole international style; the region also makes excellent Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, aromatic Riesling and Pinot Gris, plus traditional-method sparkling wine.

**Character** — A cool, sunny climate with a big day-to-night temperature swing gives wines of intense aroma and zingy acidity. Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is instantly recognisable — pungent and vivid, with passion fruit, gooseberry, fresh-cut grass and citrus.

**Good to know** — Its rise from almost nothing in the 1970s to worldwide fame is one of the great modern wine success stories, and Sauvignon Blanc remains its calling card.

name: Campania
description:
**Campania** — a region in southern Italy centred on Naples and the Amalfi coast, with a winemaking heritage stretching back to ancient Greek and Roman times. Its strength lies in distinctive native grapes.

**Wines & grapes** — The great red is Aglianico, which reaches its peak in Taurasi — a deep, structured, tannic and long-lived wine sometimes called the Barolo of the south. Among whites, Fiano di Avellino, Greco di Tufo and the softer Falanghina all make characterful, mineral wines.

**Character** — Volcanic soils around Mount Vesuvius and inland hills, plus varied altitudes, give the wines freshness, minerality and firm structure despite the warm southern climate.

**Good to know** — Campania is one of Italy's finest homes for indigenous varieties, and its top wines age remarkably well for the region's latitude.

name: Southwest France
description:
**Southwest France** — known in French as the Sud-Ouest, a loose grouping of scattered wine areas across the southwest of the country, inland and south of Bordeaux, reaching toward the Pyrenees. It is a treasure trove of local grapes found almost nowhere else.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds are the highlight: Malbec makes the dark, firm wines of Cahors, and Tannat gives the powerful, tannic reds of Madiran. Bordeaux varieties like Merlot and the Cabernets appear widely, while distinctive whites come from grapes such as Gros and Petit Manseng, notably in the sweet and dry wines of Jurançon.

**Character** — Styles are diverse but often robust and characterful, with many old regional varieties preserved here.

**Good to know** — Historically overshadowed by neighbouring Bordeaux, the region offers great value and unusual, distinctive flavours.

name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
description:
**Friuli-Venezia Giulia** is a region tucked into the northeastern corner of Italy, between the Alps and the Adriatic where it borders Slovenia and Austria. It is best known as one of the country's finest sources of white wine.

**Wines & grapes** — The reputation rests on crisp, textured whites from Friulano (the local signature), Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon, Ribolla Gialla, and Malvasia, along with aromatic Picolit dessert wines. Reds from Refosco, Schioppettino and international grapes are made too, and the region is a heartland of the amber "orange" skin-contact movement.

**Character** — Cool air off the mountains and warmth from the sea give the wines both freshness and depth, with a purity and mineral cut that has become a Friulian trademark.

**Good to know** — The top subzones Collio and Colli Orientali sit on a distinctive marl-and-sandstone soil that locals call ponca.

name: Oregon
description:
**Oregon** is a US state in the Pacific Northwest that has built an outsized wine reputation on a single grape. Its cool, green valleys have become one of the New World's benchmark homes for Pinot Noir.

**Wines & grapes** — Pinot Noir dominates, joined by excellent Pinot Gris, Chardonnay and aromatic whites such as Riesling and Gewürztraminer. The Willamette Valley, running south of Portland, is the centre of gravity, while warmer southern valleys grow a broader mix.

**Character** — A marginal, rainy, cool climate yields Pinot Noir that leans toward elegance and freshness rather than power, with red-fruit perfume and firm acidity.

**Good to know** — The industry has a strong streak of small, hands-on, sustainability-minded producers, and Burgundian houses have invested here.

name: Gisborne
description:
**Gisborne** sits on the eastern tip of New Zealand's North Island, one of the first places in the country to see the sunrise. It is known above all for white wine, and long styled itself as a Chardonnay capital.

**Wines & grapes** — Chardonnay is the flagship, typically ripe and generous, alongside aromatic whites such as Gewürztraminer, Viognier and Pinot Gris. Some Merlot and other reds are grown, but the region's heart is clearly white.

**Character** — Fertile plains and a warm, sunny maritime climate give wines that are round, fruit-forward and approachable, with softer acidity than New Zealand's cooler zones.

**Good to know** — It is a relatively warm, high-yielding area, and a fair share of its fruit has historically fed larger blended bottlings.

name: Languedoc
description:
**Languedoc** is a vast wine region sweeping along France's Mediterranean coast in the south, from the Rhône delta toward the Spanish border. Once famous mainly for volume, it is now a dynamic source of characterful, well-priced wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds lead, built on Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Carignan, with appellations such as Corbières, Minervois, Faugères and Pic Saint-Loup. It also makes rosé, herby whites, and distinctive sparkling and fortified sweet wines.

**Character** — A hot, dry, sunny climate and garrigue-scented hills give reds that are warm, spicy and full of dark fruit, often with a wild Mediterranean herbal edge.

**Good to know** — Much wine here is sold under the broad Pays d'Oc label, which allows single-varietal bottlings.

name: Washington
description:
**Washington** is a US state in the Pacific Northwest and, after California, one of America's largest wine producers. Most vineyards lie not in the rainy west but in the arid, sunny interior east of the Cascade Mountains.

**Wines & grapes** — It is a red-wine powerhouse, especially Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah, with strong Bordeaux-style blends. Whites such as Riesling and Chardonnay are also important, and Columbia Valley is the sprawling parent region.

**Character** — Hot, dry days and cold nights over irrigated desert soils produce ripe yet structured reds with deep colour, firm tannins and bright acidity.

**Good to know** — The far-northern latitude gives unusually long summer daylight, helping fruit ripen fully.

name: Abruzzo
description:
**Abruzzo** lies in central Italy on the Adriatic side, a rugged region of high Apennine mountains that drop toward the coast. It is a reliable, good-value source of both red and white wine.

**Wines & grapes** — The signature red is Montepulciano d'Abruzzo, deep and juicy, while the crisp white Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is the main white. A distinctive dark, cherry-scented rosé called Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo is also a local specialty.

**Character** — Warm coastal sun tempered by cool mountain air gives reds that are rich and smooth with soft tannins and dark-fruit flavour, and whites that stay fresh.

**Good to know** — Do not confuse the grape Montepulciano here with the Tuscan town of Montepulciano, which makes Sangiovese-based wine.

name: Clare Valley
description:
**Clare Valley** is a wine region in South Australia, north of Adelaide, set among rolling hills at relatively high elevation. It is celebrated as one of Australia's premier homes for Riesling.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling is the star, made bone-dry, and it also produces excellent Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon. The combination of a great white and serious reds from one area is part of the valley's appeal.

**Character** — Warm days and notably cool nights preserve acidity, giving Rieslings that are taut, dry and citrus-driven, famous for aging into toasty, lime-scented maturity, while the reds stay firm and structured.

**Good to know** — Clare was an early Australian adopter of the screwcap closure, championed to protect its delicate Rieslings.

name: Niagara Peninsula
description:
**Niagara Peninsula** is Canada's most important wine region, set in Ontario on the strip of land between Lake Ontario and Lake Erie near Niagara Falls. It is world-famous for one thing above all: icewine.

**Wines & grapes** — Its signature is intensely sweet icewine, made from grapes such as Vidal and Riesling frozen on the vine. Beyond that it makes fine dry Riesling and Chardonnay, plus reds and rosés from Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc and others.

**Character** — A cool, continental climate moderated by the surrounding lakes lets grapes hang late, and the reliably cold winters make natural icewine possible year after year.

**Good to know** — Canadian icewine is tightly regulated, requiring genuine natural freezing rather than artificial chilling.

name: Hunter Valley
description:
**Hunter Valley** lies in New South Wales, north of Sydney, and is the oldest continuously producing wine region in Australia. It holds a special place in the country's wine history and identity.

**Wines & grapes** — Its most distinctive wine is Semillon, picked early and made low in alcohol, and Shiraz is the classic red. Chardonnay and Verdelho are grown too, but Semillon and Shiraz define the valley's character.

**Character** — The climate is warm and humid, unusual for fine wine, yet it yields a Semillon that is light and citrusy when young and transforms with age into a honeyed, toasty white, alongside earthy, medium-bodied Shiraz.

**Good to know** — Aged Hunter Semillon is considered one of the wine world's great, and most unlikely, cellar treasures.

name: Jura
description:
**Jura** is a small, mountainous French wine region east of Burgundy, near the Swiss border. Though tiny, it has a devoted following for its highly distinctive and unusual wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Whites come from Chardonnay and the local Savagnin; reds and rosés from Poulsard, Trousseau and Pinot Noir. Its most famous style is Vin Jaune, a nutty, sherry-like white aged under a film of yeast, plus the sweet straw wine Vin de Paille and the sparkling Crémant du Jura.

**Character** — A cool climate and marl soils, combined with deliberate oxidative aging, give many wines a savoury, nutty, curry-spice complexity unlike anywhere else.

**Good to know** — Vin Jaune is bottled in the distinctive squat 62 cl clavelin.

name: Lombardy
description:
**Lombardy** is a large, wealthy region in northern Italy centred on Milan, stretching from the Alps to the Po plain. It is home to some of Italy's most prestigious sparkling wine and a distinctive mountain red.

**Wines & grapes** — Franciacorta, made by the traditional bottle-fermented method from Chardonnay and Pinot Nero, is the flagship and rivals fine Champagne. Valtellina in the Alpine north grows Nebbiolo (locally Chiavennasca), while Oltrepò Pavese produces a broad range of still and sparkling wines.

**Character** — Cool, varied terrain gives elegant, high-acid sparkling wines and, in Valtellina, lighter, aromatic, high-altitude Nebbiolo grown on steep terraces.

**Good to know** — Sforzato di Valtellina is a powerful dry red made from dried grapes, like a Nebbiolo take on Amarone.

name: Quebec
description:
**Quebec** is a cold, northern province of eastern Canada with a small but growing wine industry, concentrated south of Montreal near the US border. Its winemakers work at the frigid edge of where grapes can ripen.

**Wines & grapes** — Much of the vineyard is planted to cold-hardy hybrid varieties bred to survive harsh winters, producing dry whites, rosés and light reds. The province is especially known for sweet winter specialties, including icewine and its distinctive ice cider.

**Character** — A short growing season and brutal winters shape the wines, which tend to be light, fresh and high in acidity, with the cold turned to advantage in the dessert styles.

**Good to know** — Some growers physically bury or protect their vines to help them survive the deep winter freeze.

name: Provence
description:
**Provence** ... — a sun-drenched region in the far south-east of France, running along the Mediterranean coast, and the spiritual home of dry rosé.

**Wines & grapes** — Above all pale, dry rosé, typically blended from Grenache, Cinsault, Syrah and Mourvèdre. There are serious reds too, and a small amount of white; the coastal appellation of Bandol is prized for structured, age-worthy Mourvèdre-based reds, while Cassis is known for its whites.

**Character** — The classic Provençal rosé is very pale, almost onion-skin pink, with crisp acidity and gentle notes of red berry, citrus and herbs. A warm, dry climate and cooling sea breezes shape the freshness.

**Good to know** — Côtes de Provence is the largest appellation, and the region has done more than any other to make dry rosé a fashionable, year-round drink.

name: Niederösterreich
description:
**Niederösterreich** ... — Lower Austria, the country's largest quality wine region, spread across the north-east around the Danube and its tributaries.

**Wines & grapes** — Predominantly crisp, dry whites, led by Grüner Veltliner, Austria's signature grape, and fine Riesling. It contains celebrated sub-zones such as the Wachau, Kremstal and Kamptal, along with reds from around Vienna's fringes.

**Character** — Cool continental conditions and steep terraced vineyards give whites with bright acidity, mineral drive and, in the case of Grüner Veltliner, a distinctive peppery, citrus-and-green-herb note. The best examples age gracefully.

**Good to know** — The steep Wachau terraces along the Danube are among Austria's most scenic and highly regarded vineyard sites.

name: Swartland
description:
**Swartland** ... — a warm, dry-farmed region north of Cape Town in South Africa's Western Cape, and one of the country's most exciting sources of characterful wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Old-vine Chenin Blanc is a calling card, alongside Rhône-inspired reds and whites built on Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre, Cinsault and other Mediterranean varieties.

**Character** — Hot summers, granite and shale soils, and many old bush vines yield concentrated, textured wines. A wave of independent, minimal-intervention producers has given the area a reputation for expressive, terroir-focused bottlings rather than heavy, over-oaked styles.

**Good to know** — Once known mainly for bulk wine and wheat, Swartland's revival over the past couple of decades has made it a byword for South African quality and originality.

name: Ahr
description:
**Ahr** ... — one of Germany's smallest and most northerly wine regions, following the Ahr river valley south of Bonn, and unusually devoted to red wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Chiefly Pinot Noir, known here as Spätburgunder, with some Portugieser and a little white. It is one of the rare German regions where red dominates.

**Character** — Steep, slate and volcanic slopes trap warmth in a cool northern setting, producing red wines that are typically elegant, silky and relatively light-bodied, with red-cherry fruit and fine structure.

**Good to know** — Despite the northern latitude, the sheltered, sun-catching valley walls make ripe red wine possible, and the Ahr's Pinot Noir has a devoted following.

name: Burgenland
description:
**Burgenland** ... — a wine region in eastern Austria, along the Hungarian border, best known for its red wines and world-class sweet whites.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds built on Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt lead the way, while the area around the shallow Lake Neusiedl is famous for luscious botrytis-affected dessert wines.

**Character** — A warm, sunny, Pannonian climate ripens reds fully, giving wines with dark fruit, spice and firm but supple structure. The lake's humidity encourages noble rot, ideal for concentrated sweet wines.

**Good to know** — Burgenland is the heartland of Austria's red-wine renaissance, with Blaufränkisch increasingly seen as its most serious and age-worthy variety.

name: Franken
description:
**Franken** ... — a region in northern Bavaria, in southern Germany, set along the Main river around Würzburg, with a strong identity of its own.

**Wines & grapes** — Dry whites are the focus, and Silvaner is the signature grape, alongside Müller-Thurgau and Riesling. Reds are a minor presence.

**Character** — A cooler, more continental climate and varied soils give wines that are typically dry, earthy and firmly structured rather than fruity or floral, with Silvaner showing a distinctive savoury, minerally profile.

**Good to know** — Many Franken wines are bottled in the traditional flask-shaped Bocksbeutel, a rounded flattened bottle that makes them instantly recognisable on the shelf.

name: Ontario
description:
**Ontario** ... — Canada's largest wine province, with vineyards concentrated near the Great Lakes, most famously on the Niagara Peninsula.

**Wines & grapes** — A cool-climate mix of Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Franc, plus sparkling wine. Ontario is especially renowned for icewine, often from Vidal and Riesling.

**Character** — The moderating effect of the lakes tempers a cold continental climate, allowing grapes to ripen while retaining bright acidity. Reliably freezing winters make Ontario one of the world's most consistent producers of intensely sweet, concentrated icewine.

**Good to know** — Genuine icewine is made from grapes left to freeze on the vine and pressed while frozen, and Ontario's cold winters give it a global reputation for the style.

name: Roussillon
description:
**Roussillon** ... — a warm, mountainous region in the far south of France, hugging the Mediterranean coast and the Spanish border near the eastern Pyrenees.

**Wines & grapes** — Rich dry reds and whites built on Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre and Carignan, plus a proud tradition of fortified sweet wines (vins doux naturels) such as Banyuls, Maury and Rivesaltes.

**Character** — Intense sunshine, low rainfall, dramatic schist and granite terraces, and old bush vines produce concentrated, full-bodied wines. The fortified sweet wines, made from very ripe Grenache, range from fresh and grapey to deep, nutty and oxidative.

**Good to know** — Catalan culture runs deep here, and Roussillon is one of France's most important sources of traditional fortified wine.

name: Beaujolais
description:
**Beaujolais** ... — a region in eastern France, just south of Burgundy, devoted almost entirely to juicy, food-friendly red wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Almost all red, made from the Gamay grape, ranging from light everyday bottlings to the more structured wines of the ten named Crus such as Morgon, Fleurie and Moulin-à-Vent.

**Character** — Granite soils in the north and a gentle climate give reds that are bright, fresh and low in tannin, bursting with red-berry fruit and floral notes; the Crus can add depth and the ability to age.

**Good to know** — Beaujolais Nouveau, released each November just weeks after harvest, made the region famous, but its serious Crus deserve far more attention.

name: Umbria
description:
**Umbria** ... — a landlocked region in central Italy, tucked beside Tuscany, sometimes called the country's green heart.

**Wines & grapes** — Best known for the powerful red Sagrantino di Montefalco, made from the local Sagrantino grape, and for the crisp white Orvieto, based largely on Grechetto and Trebbiano. Sangiovese also features widely.

**Character** — Hilly inland vineyards and a warm but continental climate give a mix of structured, deeply coloured reds and fresh, easygoing whites. Sagrantino is notably tannic and long-lived, one of Italy's most robust native reds.

**Good to know** — Montefalco Sagrantino was once made mainly as a sweet passito wine, but today the dry version is Umbria's flagship.

name: Alentejo
description:
**Alentejo** ... — a vast, warm, sparsely populated region covering much of southern Portugal, inland from Lisbon.

**Wines & grapes** — Mostly generous, ripe reds from native varieties such as Aragonez (Tempranillo), Trincadeira, Alicante Bouschet and Touriga Nacional, along with fuller-bodied whites from grapes like Antão Vaz and Arinto.

**Character** — Hot, dry summers and rolling plains produce soft, fruit-forward, approachable reds with smooth tannins and warm spice. The region is also known for reviving the ancient tradition of fermenting wine in large clay amphorae, called talha.

**Good to know** — Alentejo is one of Portugal's most commercially successful regions, popular for its easy, crowd-pleasing style and good value.

name: Alto Adige (Südtirol)
description:
**Alto Adige (Südtirol)** ... — a small alpine region in Italy's far north, in the German-speaking province of South Tyrol, where valley vineyards climb steep mountain slopes.

**Wines & grapes** — Best known for precise, aromatic whites such as Pinot Grigio, Pinot Bianco, Gewürztraminer and Chardonnay, plus reds from the local Schiava (Vernatsch) and Lagrein.

**Character** — High altitude, big day-to-night temperature swings and abundant sunshine give whites with crystalline purity, bright acidity and clear varietal aromas. Lagrein makes a dark, structured red, while Schiava is light and easy.

**Good to know** — The region's dual Italian-German identity is reflected in its bilingual wine names, and it is regarded as one of Italy's top sources of crisp mountain whites.

name: Central Valley
description:
**Central Valley** — Chile's vast winemaking heartland, a long stretch of vineyards running south from near Santiago between the Andes and the coastal range. It supplies the bulk of the country's exported wine and takes in celebrated sub-zones such as Maipo, Colchagua, Curicó and Maule.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds dominate, led by Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and the country's signature Carmenère, with plenty of Syrah too. Whites come mainly from Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.

**Character** — A warm, dry Mediterranean climate with reliable sunshine and cool nights, watered by snowmelt channelled down from the Andes. The wines tend to be ripe, generous and fruit-forward, offering dependable quality at every price level.

**Good to know** — Carmenère, long confused with Merlot in these vineyards, has become Chile's calling-card grape.

name: Marche
description:
**Marche** — A region on Italy's central Adriatic coast, tucked between the Apennine mountains and the sea. It is best known for crisp white wines built on the Verdicchio grape.

**Wines & grapes** — Verdicchio is the star, giving fresh, savoury whites in zones such as Castelli di Jesi and Matelica. Reds lean on Montepulciano and Sangiovese, seen in appellations like Rosso Conero and Rosso Piceno.

**Character** — Hillsides catch both sea breezes and mountain air, producing whites with a lively citrus edge and a characteristic almond note on the finish, and reds that are supple and approachable.

name: Emilia-Romagna
description:
**Emilia-Romagna** — A large region spanning north-central Italy, from the Apennine foothills across a broad plain to the Adriatic. It is most famous internationally for Lambrusco, the lightly sparkling red.

**Wines & grapes** — Lambrusco leads, made in styles from bone dry to sweet, all with a refreshing fizz. Romagna to the east contributes Sangiovese reds and the white grapes Albana and Pignoletto.

**Character** — Fertile plains and rolling hills give mostly easy-drinking, food-friendly wines. Lambrusco's bright acidity and frothy texture make it a natural partner for the region's rich cured meats and cheeses.

**Good to know** — Albana di Romagna was Italy's first white wine to earn DOCG status.

name: Castilla-La Mancha
description:
**Castilla-La Mancha** — A sprawling, sun-baked plateau in central Spain south of Madrid, home to the largest concentration of vineyards on earth. Its heartland is the La Mancha appellation, alongside zones such as Valdepeñas.

**Wines & grapes** — The white Airén, planted here in huge quantity, and the red Tempranillo (locally called Cencibel) are the mainstays, joined by Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon and others.

**Character** — A harsh continental climate of blazing summers and cold winters over high, arid ground. Long the source of inexpensive bulk wine, the region increasingly turns out serious, value-driven reds.

**Good to know** — Several single-estate Vino de Pago wines here carry Spain's highest quality designation.

name: Peloponnese
description:
**Peloponnese** — A large peninsula forming the southern tip of mainland Greece, and one of the country's most important areas for quality wine. It holds historic appellations such as Nemea, Mantinia and Patras.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds come chiefly from Agiorgitiko, grown around Nemea, while the aromatic white Moschofilero shines in the cooler highlands of Mantinia. Roditis and sweet Muscat from Patras add further variety.

**Character** — Landscapes range from warm coastal plains to cool mountain vineyards at altitude, yielding everything from soft, juicy reds to fresh, floral whites. The native grapes give the wines a distinctly Greek personality.

name: Central Coast
description:
**Central Coast** — A long California wine region running down the Pacific coast from the San Francisco Bay area to Santa Barbara. It spans a huge range of climates and includes noted zones like Paso Robles, Santa Lucia Highlands, Edna Valley and Santa Barbara.

**Wines & grapes** — Its breadth supports many grapes: cool coastal spots excel with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, while warmer inland sites favour Syrah and other Rhône varieties, Cabernet Sauvignon and Zinfandel.

**Character** — Fog and ocean influence cool the seaside vineyards, while inland valleys ripen richer, fuller reds. This variety of sites makes it one of California's most diverse growing regions.

name: Aragón
description:
**Aragón** — A region in north-eastern Spain, inland from Catalonia, regarded as one of the great homes of the Garnacha grape. Its wines come from appellations such as Campo de Borja, Calatayud, Cariñena and Somontano.

**Wines & grapes** — Old-vine Garnacha is the calling card, producing deep, warming reds, often blended with Tempranillo, Syrah or Cariñena. Somontano, in the Pyrenean foothills, also makes fresher reds and whites from international varieties.

**Character** — A dry continental climate with hot days and cold nights over stony, poor soils yields concentrated, robust reds that offer excellent value for money.

name: New York
description:
**New York** — A cool-climate wine region in the north-eastern United States, and one of the country's older winegrowing areas. Its key districts are the Finger Lakes, Long Island and the Hudson River Valley.

**Wines & grapes** — The Finger Lakes are celebrated for Riesling, together with other aromatic whites and Pinot Noir, while maritime Long Island focuses on Bordeaux grapes such as Merlot and Cabernet Franc. Native and hybrid varieties are grown too.

**Character** — Deep lakes and coastal waters moderate the cold, letting grapes ripen through a short, cool season. The whites are marked by bright acidity and precision.

**Good to know** — Finger Lakes Riesling is widely rated among America's finest.

name: Nelson
description:
**Nelson** — A small, sunny wine region at the northern tip of New Zealand's South Island, just west of Marlborough, with a strong boutique, artisan character.

**Wines & grapes** — Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay lead the whites, with excellent aromatic Riesling and Pinot Gris, while Pinot Noir is the main red.

**Character** — A cool but bright maritime climate with plenty of sunshine hours gives wines with vibrant fruit and crisp acidity. Production is small in scale and firmly quality-focused.

name: Canterbury
description:
**Canterbury** — A wine region on the east coast of New Zealand's South Island, around Christchurch, with the Waipara Valley as its best-known sub-district.

**Wines & grapes** — Pinot Noir and Riesling are the standouts, supported by Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Gris.

**Character** — A cool, relatively dry climate with a long ripening season produces elegant, aromatic whites and finely structured Pinot Noir. Waipara's warmer, sheltered sites add a little extra ripeness.

name: Texas
description:
**Texas** — A growing wine region in the southern United States, and one of the country's larger producers by volume. Most vineyards lie in the High Plains around Lubbock and in the Hill Country at the centre of the state.

**Wines & grapes** — Warm-climate grapes do best, with Tempranillo, Mourvèdre, Sangiovese and Viognier among the varieties suited to the heat, alongside other Rhône and Mediterranean styles.

**Character** — A hot, sunny climate tempered by high-altitude sites and cool nights on the plains gives ripe, full-bodied wines. The industry is young but improving quickly.

name: New South Wales
description:
**New South Wales** — A major wine state in south-eastern Australia, home to the historic Hunter Valley and a spread of other districts including Riverina, Mudgee, Orange and the Canberra District.

**Wines & grapes** — The Hunter is famous for long-lived Semillon and earthy Shiraz, while Riverina is known for luscious botrytis-affected sweet Semillon. Cooler, higher zones like Orange and Canberra add Chardonnay, Riesling and Shiraz.

**Character** — Styles vary widely with climate, from the humid, subtropical Hunter to cool, elevated inland sites. Hunter Semillon, picked early and aged in bottle, is one of Australia's most distinctive whites.

**Good to know** — The Hunter Valley is among the oldest wine regions in Australia.

name: Santa Barbara County
description:
**Santa Barbara County** — On California's Central Coast, north of Los Angeles, this is one of the state's most distinctive cool-climate zones, thanks to valleys that run east to west and funnel Pacific fog straight inland. It reached a wider audience after the film *Sideways* put its Pinot Noir in the spotlight.

**Wines & grapes** — Pinot Noir and Chardonnay are the calling cards, grown in cooler sub-areas such as the Santa Rita Hills and Santa Maria Valley. Warmer pockets also do well with Syrah and other Rhône grapes.

**Character** — The unusual transverse valleys draw in ocean air, giving long, slow ripening that keeps acidity fresh and flavours precise. Wines tend toward elegance rather than heft.

**Good to know** — The Santa Rita Hills in particular is prized for taut, mineral Pinot Noir.

name: Paso Robles
description:
**Paso Robles** — Also on California's Central Coast but well inland, Paso Robles is a warm, sprawling region known for generous, sun-filled reds and a pioneering streak with Rhône grape varieties.

**Wines & grapes** — Zinfandel is a longtime staple, alongside Cabernet Sauvignon and Rhône varieties such as Syrah and Grenache, often blended. Whites like Viognier and Roussanne are made too.

**Character** — Hot days and notably cool nights — a wide daily temperature swing — let grapes ripen fully while holding on to acidity, producing bold, ripe, fruit-forward wines. The region is large and varied, from cooler limestone-rich hills in the west to warmer flats in the east.

**Good to know** — It became a hub for the "Rhône Rangers" movement championing Syrah and Grenache in California.

name: Galicia
description:
**Galicia** — In Spain's rainy, green northwest corner, on the Atlantic coast above Portugal, Galicia is celebrated above all for crisp, aromatic white wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Albariño, grown mainly in Rías Baixas near the sea, is the signature — bright and citrusy. Inland areas make excellent whites from Godello and reds from Mencía, notably in Ribeira Sacra and Valdeorras.

**Character** — The cool, wet, ocean-influenced climate — quite unlike the dry Spanish interior — gives wines high natural acidity, freshness and a saline lift that pairs beautifully with the region's seafood.

name: South Eastern Australia
description:
**South Eastern Australia** — This is not a single place but a very large official zone covering most of Australia's vineyard land, stretching across several states. It exists mainly as a labelling category for blended wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Because grapes can be sourced from anywhere within the zone, wines span the full range — Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and more — usually made in an approachable, consistent style.

**Character** — The name signals a wine blended across regions for reliability and value rather than a specific local identity, and it appears often on well-known everyday brands.

name: Setúbal Peninsula
description:
**Setúbal Peninsula** — Just south of Lisbon in Portugal, this coastal region is best known for a historic fortified sweet wine, though it makes plenty of dry table wine too.

**Wines & grapes** — Its fame rests on Moscatel de Setúbal, a rich, aromatic fortified wine from Muscat grapes. Dry reds lean on Castelão and international varieties, with whites from Fernão Pires and others.

**Character** — A warm, sunny, maritime climate suits both the honeyed, orange-peel intensity of the Moscatel and ripe, easy-drinking reds. The fortified wines can age remarkably well, deepening in colour and complexity.

name: Western Australia
description:
**Western Australia** — Occupying the country's vast western third, this state produces only a small share of Australia's wine but a high proportion of its most acclaimed bottles.

**Wines & grapes** — The standout grapes are Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay, with fine Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc and Semillon as well. Margaret River is the best-known region, joined by the cooler Great Southern.

**Character** — Many of the top areas enjoy a maritime climate moderated by the surrounding oceans, favouring structured, elegant wines with good balance rather than sheer power.

name: Liguria
description:
**Liguria** — A thin, mountainous arc along Italy's northwest coast — the Italian Riviera — Liguria makes small quantities of distinctive wine on steep terraces above the sea.

**Wines & grapes** — Whites dominate, chiefly Vermentino and Pigato, both crisp and herb-scented. Reds come from Rossese, notably around Dolceacqua, and the Cinque Terre is famous for its rare sweet Sciacchetrà.

**Character** — Vineyards clinging to sheer coastal slopes, sea breezes and poor soils yield fresh, mineral, saline wines. Production is tiny and much of it is drunk locally, so bottles are prized finds.

name: Colchagua Valley
description:
**Colchagua Valley** — Part of the larger Rapel Valley in Chile's Central Valley, Colchagua is one of the country's premier zones for full-bodied red wine.

**Wines & grapes** — It is red-wine country above all — Cabernet Sauvignon, Carmenère, Syrah and Malbec — with the Apalta sub-area especially renowned for concentrated, age-worthy blends.

**Character** — A warm, sunny valley climate cooled by ocean and mountain influences produces ripe, deeply coloured, richly fruited reds with firm structure. Carmenère, Chile's signature grape, thrives here.

name: Valais
description:
**Valais** — In the sunny upper Rhône valley of southern Switzerland, Valais is the country's largest and one of its most varied wine regions, farmed on dramatic Alpine terraces.

**Wines & grapes** — The workhorse white is Chasselas (known locally as Fendant), while Pinot Noir and Gamay make the red blend called Dôle. Valais is also a treasury of rare native grapes such as Petite Arvine, Amigne, Humagne and Cornalin.

**Character** — Steep, sun-drenched slopes and a dry mountain climate give wines that are ripe yet fresh, ranging from easy-drinking whites to characterful, distinctly local specialties. Little leaves Switzerland, so these bottles are seldom seen abroad.

name: Pennsylvania
description:
**Pennsylvania** — A state in the northeastern United States with a small but growing wine industry spread across many family-run wineries.

**Wines & grapes** — Growers work with a mix of hybrid grapes such as Chambourcin and cold-hardy classic varieties like Riesling, Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc, producing everything from dry table wines to sweeter styles.

**Character** — A cool, humid continental climate makes grape-growing a challenge, so hardy varieties and careful site selection matter. The wines are mostly enjoyed regionally rather than widely exported.

name: Trentino-Alto Adige
description:
**Trentino-Alto Adige** — Italy's northernmost wine region, tucked into the Alps near the Austrian border, combines two provinces: Italian-speaking Trentino and German-speaking Alto Adige (Südtirol).

**Wines & grapes** — It is celebrated for crisp, aromatic whites — Pinot Grigio, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Bianco and Chardonnay — and for local reds such as Teroldego, Lagrein and the light Schiava. Trentino is also a source of fine traditional-method sparkling wine (Trentodoc).

**Character** — High-altitude vineyards on Alpine slopes, cool nights and bright sunshine give wines of vivid freshness, purity and definition, especially the whites. The two provinces share geography but each keeps its own cultural and stylistic accent.

name: Margaret River
description:
**Margaret River** — A maritime region in the far southwest of Western Australia, Margaret River is one of the country's most prestigious wine areas despite producing only a small fraction of its total output.

**Wines & grapes** — It is renowned for structured, Bordeaux-style Cabernet Sauvignon and for refined Chardonnay, plus a distinctive blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Semillon.

**Character** — Cooled and moderated by the Indian and Southern Oceans, with well-drained gravelly soils, the climate yields wines of elegance, balance and consistency. Quality is high and reputations well established.

**Good to know** — Its Cabernet and Chardonnay regularly rank among Australia's finest.

name: Lehigh Valley
description:
**Lehigh Valley** ... — a wine-growing area in eastern Pennsylvania, United States, spread across the rolling farmland north of Philadelphia. It is one of the more established grape-growing pockets of the American Northeast.

**Wines & grapes** — Producers here work with a mix of cold-hardy hybrids and classic European varieties. Whites such as Riesling and Chardonnay, and reds including Cabernet Franc, are grown alongside hybrid grapes bred to survive harsh winters, and both dry table wines and off-dry styles are made.

**Character** — This is a cool, continental climate with cold winters and warm, humid summers, so growers favour varieties that ripen reliably and resist frost. The wines tend toward brighter acidity and moderate alcohol, and the region reflects the broader revival of serious winemaking in the eastern United States.

name: Jalisco
description:
**Jalisco** ... — a state in western Mexico, far better known as the heartland of tequila production than as a wine region. A small amount of grape wine is nonetheless made in its highland areas.

**Wines & grapes** — Wine here is a niche pursuit compared with agave spirits. The higher-elevation zones grow international varieties, and small producers make modest quantities of red and white table wine.

**Character** — Elevation is the key moderating factor, tempering the warmth of this southerly latitude so that grapes can hold their balance. Wine remains a minor and emerging part of Jalisco's drinks culture, which is dominated by tequila from the town of Tequila and the surrounding agave fields.

name: Tokaj
description:
**Tokaj** ... — a historic wine region in northeastern Hungary, extending slightly into Slovakia, and one of the world's most celebrated sources of sweet wine. Its name is attached to the legendary Tokaji Aszú.

**Wines & grapes** — The signature style is Tokaji Aszú, made from grapes shrivelled by noble rot (botrytis) and measured historically in puttonyos of sweetness. Furmint is the leading grape, joined by Hárslevelű, Sárgamuskotály (Yellow Muscat) and others; the region also makes late-harvest Szamorodni and, increasingly, crisp dry whites from Furmint.

**Character** — Volcanic soils, the meeting of the Bodrog and Tisza rivers, and autumn mists create ideal conditions for botrytis. The sweet wines are famous for their honeyed apricot and marmalade richness balanced by piercing acidity, giving them remarkable longevity.

**Good to know** — Tokaji was prized at European royal courts and is sometimes called the "wine of kings."

name: Northern Rhône
description:
**Northern Rhône** ... — the upper stretch of France's Rhône Valley, running south from around Vienne along steep slopes above the river. It is one of the great homes of Syrah.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds are made almost entirely from Syrah, in appellations such as Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Cornas and Crozes-Hermitage. Small amounts of Viognier may be co-fermented with Syrah in Côte-Rôtie, while whites come from Viognier (notably in Condrieu) plus Marsanne and Roussanne.

**Character** — The vineyards cling to precipitous granite terraces that catch the sun, and the climate is more continental than the south. The best reds are deeply coloured and structured, with notes often described as black pepper, smoked meat and dark fruit, and they age superbly.

**Good to know** — Hermitage and Côte-Rôtie are among the most collectible and long-lived wines of France.

name: Macedonia
description:
**Macedonia** ... — a large region in northern Greece stretching from the Aegean coast toward the mountainous interior. It is one of the country's most important sources of serious red wine.

**Wines & grapes** — The flagship grape is Xinomavro, the backbone of appellations such as Naoussa and Amyndeon, giving structured, age-worthy reds. Other local and international varieties are grown too, and the region produces still reds, rosés and some whites.

**Character** — Climate ranges from warmer coastal zones to cooler, higher-altitude sites inland. Xinomavro is prized for its firm tannins, high acidity and savoury tomato-and-herb character, and it is often compared to Nebbiolo for its structure and capacity to age.

name: Martinborough
description:
**Martinborough** ... — a small, highly regarded wine town in the Wairarapa district at the southern end of New Zealand's North Island. It built its reputation on one grape above all.

**Wines & grapes** — Pinot Noir is the star here, producing wines of finesse and concentration. Aromatic whites also do well, including Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Riesling and some Chardonnay.

**Character** — Free-draining gravel terraces, low rainfall and cool, breezy conditions give small yields and intensely flavoured fruit. The Pinot Noirs are typically perfumed and silky with fine tannins, and Martinborough is regarded as one of New Zealand's benchmark regions for the variety despite its modest size.

name: Adelaide Hills
description:
**Adelaide Hills** ... — a cool-climate wine region in the hills just east of the city of Adelaide in South Australia. It is one of Australia's leading sources of elegant, restrained styles.

**Wines & grapes** — Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay are widely planted, along with Pinot Noir, and the cool conditions also make it a fine base for sparkling wine. Aromatic whites and cooler-climate Shiraz are made as well.

**Character** — Elevation brings cooler temperatures and a longer growing season than the surrounding warm plains, preserving acidity and delicacy. The wines are known for their freshness, bright fruit and finer structure, offering a contrast to the bolder reds of nearby regions such as the Barossa and McLaren Vale.

name: Lazio
description:
**Lazio** ... — a central Italian region surrounding Rome, stretching from the Tyrrhenian coast to the Apennine foothills. It is best known for the everyday white wines poured in the capital.

**Wines & grapes** — The classic style is Frascati, a dry white based on Malvasia and Trebbiano grown in the volcanic hills south of Rome. The region also makes other whites and a growing amount of red wine from both local and international grapes.

**Character** — Volcanic soils and a warm Mediterranean climate shape wines that are typically fresh, soft and approachable in youth. While long associated with simple carafe whites, Lazio has seen quality-focused producers raise the profile of both its whites and reds in recent years.

name: Murcia
description:
**Murcia** ... — an autonomous region in southeastern Spain, inland from the Mediterranean coast. It is a warm, sun-drenched area that has become known for full-bodied reds.

**Wines & grapes** — Monastrell (the grape known elsewhere as Mourvèdre) is the dominant variety, forming the core of denominations such as Jumilla, Yecla and Bullas. It yields deeply coloured, powerful reds, with rosés and some whites also produced.

**Character** — The climate is hot and dry with poor soils and low rainfall, conditions that stress the vines and concentrate the fruit. The wines are typically rich and ripe, with dark berry flavours and generous alcohol, and the region offers notable value for boldly styled Mediterranean reds.

name: Waiheke Island
description:
**Waiheke Island** ... — an island in the Hauraki Gulf a short ferry ride from Auckland, in New Zealand's warmer north. It is a boutique region known for premium reds in a country better known for white wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Unusually for New Zealand, the island specialises in Bordeaux-style blends of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc, along with impressive Syrah. Chardonnay and other whites are grown as well.

**Character** — Surrounded by sea and enjoying a warm, sheltered maritime microclimate, Waiheke ripens red varieties that struggle in cooler parts of the country. Vineyards are small and land is scarce, so the wines are made in limited quantities and command premium prices, matching the island's reputation as an upmarket getaway.

name: Southern Rhône
description:
**Southern Rhône** ... — the broad, sun-baked lower section of France's Rhône Valley, spreading out around Avignon and Orange. It is the volume heart of the Rhône and home to some of its most famous appellations.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds are typically blends led by Grenache, supported by Syrah, Mourvèdre and other varieties. Châteauneuf-du-Pape is the flagship, alongside Gigondas, Vacqueyras and the vast Côtes du Rhône; the region also makes rosé (notably nearby Tavel) and some whites.

**Character** — The climate is warmer and drier than the north, swept by the fierce Mistral wind, and famous sites are covered in large rounded stones (galets) that retain heat. The reds are generous and warming, with ripe red-fruit and garrigue-herb character.

**Good to know** — Châteauneuf-du-Pape permits an unusually wide roster of grape varieties in its blends.

name: Salta
description:
**Salta** ... — a province in the far northwest of Argentina, home to some of the highest-altitude vineyards in the world. Its wines have a distinctive intensity born of extreme elevation.

**Wines & grapes** — The signature grape is Torrontés, an aromatic white that reaches its finest expression here, especially around the Cafayate valley. Malbec is the leading red, joined by Cabernet Sauvignon and other varieties.

**Character** — Vineyards planted high in the Andes — in places well over a thousand metres above sea level — bask in intense sunlight and cool nights, a combination that yields fruit with deep colour, firm acidity and pronounced aromatics. The Torrontés is floral and perfumed yet crisp, while the reds are concentrated and boldly flavoured.

name: Skåne
description:
**Skåne** is the southernmost province of Sweden and the heart of the country's small but fast-growing wine scene.

**Wines & grapes** — Growers here lean on cold-hardy hybrid and PIWI varieties such as Solaris, along with Rondo and Regent for the reds; crisp whites and traditional-method sparkling wines are the calling cards.

**Character** — This is genuine cool-climate viticulture at a high northern latitude, so the wines tend to be light-bodied, low in alcohol and bright with acidity. The short, mild summers and long daylight hours favour early-ripening grapes, and the whole region has the youthful, experimental feel of a wine culture still finding its feet.

name: Penedès
description:
**Penedès** sits in Catalonia in north-east Spain, inland from Barcelona, and is best known as the homeland of Cava, Spain's traditional-method sparkling wine.

**Wines & grapes** — The classic sparkling blend rests on the local trio of Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada, while still wines range from crisp whites to reds made from both Spanish and international grapes such as Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

**Character** — Vineyards climb from the coastal plain up to cooler hillside terraces, and that spread of altitudes lets growers ripen everything from fresh sparkling-base whites to fuller reds. Penedès has long had a reputation for innovation and was an early Spanish adopter of modern winemaking and international varieties.

name: Aegean Islands
description:
**Aegean Islands** is a Greek wine region covering the scattered islands of the Aegean Sea, including celebrated names like Santorini and Samos.

**Wines & grapes** — The signature white is Assyrtiko, famous from Santorini for its steely intensity, while Samos is renowned for sweet Muscat. Reds and other whites appear across islands such as Limnos and Rhodes.

**Character** — These are sun-drenched, wind-swept vineyards on volcanic and rocky soils, often worked in low, basket-trained forms that shield the vines from fierce Aegean gusts. The result is wines of high acidity, distinct minerality and a clear sense of their island origins.

**Good to know** — On Santorini, vines are famously coiled into low baskets called *kouloura* to protect the fruit from wind and sun.

name: Andalusia
description:
**Andalusia** is Spain's hot, sunny south, and its most famous contribution to the wine world is Sherry, the fortified wine from around Jerez.

**Wines & grapes** — Palomino is the backbone of dry Sherry styles like Fino and Amontillado, while Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel go into the intensely sweet, dark versions. The region also makes Montilla-Moriles and Málaga wines in a similar mould.

**Character** — The blazing climate and chalky white *albariza* soils are ideal for fortified wines, and the region's genius lies in how they are aged: biologically under a protective veil of *flor* yeast, or oxidatively for the darker styles, with barrels blended over time through the layered solera system.

**Good to know** — *Flor*, a living film of yeast, is what gives Fino and Manzanilla their tangy, saline freshness.

name: Sardinia
description:
**Sardinia** is a large Mediterranean island belonging to Italy, with a distinctive wine identity shaped by centuries of Spanish and local influence.

**Wines & grapes** — Cannonau, the island's name for Grenache, makes warm, generous reds, while Vermentino produces fresh, aromatic whites, especially in the north. Carignano thrives in the sandy soils of the south.

**Character** — Sun, sea breezes and varied terrain — from coastal sands to granite hills — give the wines both ripeness and lift. Sardinian reds are typically full and herb-scented, and the whites carry a saline, citrusy freshness that reflects the maritime setting.

name: Robertson
description:
**Robertson** lies inland in South Africa's Western Cape, in the Breede River valley, and has built its reputation especially on white wine.

**Wines & grapes** — Chardonnay is the local star, but the region also turns out good Sauvignon Blanc and Colombard, along with increasingly serious Shiraz and other reds.

**Character** — Robertson is unusual for the Cape in having lime-rich soils, which suit both vines and — historically — the horse studs the valley was known for. The climate is warm and dry, but cooling breezes drawn up the valley help preserve freshness, giving the Chardonnays a balance of ripe fruit and lively acidity.

name: Yarra Valley
description:
