**Geelong** is a cool-climate wine region in Victoria, Australia, spread across the countryside southwest of Melbourne near the shores of Port Phillip Bay and Bass Strait.

**Wines & grapes** — It is best known for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, along with peppery, cool-grown Shiraz and some aromatic whites.

**Character** — The maritime setting brings breezy, moderate conditions and a fairly dry climate, which suits varieties that reward a long, gentle ripening season. Wines tend to show good structure, savoury complexity and lively acidity, and the region has earned a strong following for its Pinot in particular.

name: Hainaut
description:
**Hainaut** is a province in Wallonia, the French-speaking south of Belgium, and part of the country's small but growing modern wine scene.

**Wines & grapes** — Production is modest and focused on cool-climate styles, including sparkling wines and light whites from varieties suited to a northern climate.

**Character** — This is a marginal, cool region where careful site selection and a warming climate have made quality wine increasingly possible. Output is small-scale, and the wines tend toward freshness and delicacy rather than power.

name: Bugey, Ain
description:
**Bugey, Ain** refers to the Bugey wine area in the Ain department of eastern France, tucked between Savoie, the Jura and the southern edge of Burgundy.

**Wines & grapes** — Bugey makes reds, whites, rosés and, most famously, sparkling wines. Its best-known specialty is a lightly sparkling, sweet pink wine made largely from Gamay and Poulsard. Still wines come from Gamay, Pinot Noir and Mondeuse for reds, and Chardonnay and Altesse (Roussette) for whites.

**Character** — A cool, foothill climate near the Alps gives the wines lively acidity and a fresh, mountain-fruited charm. Production is small and much of it is enjoyed locally, making Bugey something of an insider's find.

name: Kremstal
description:
**Kremstal** is a leading white-wine region in Lower Austria, set along the Danube around the town of Krems, immediately downstream from the famous Wachau and next to Kamptal.

**Wines & grapes** — The two great grapes are Grüner Veltliner, giving peppery, citrusy whites, and Riesling, producing more mineral, stone-fruited styles. Both range from crisp and everyday to concentrated, age-worthy bottlings.

**Character** — Vineyards split between deep, wind-blown loess soils and rockier terraced slopes, with the river moderating the climate and warm days meeting cool nights. The result is dry, precise, structured whites.

**Good to know** — It sits within Austria's celebrated stretch of Danube wine country, so its top wines share the freshness and longevity of their better-known neighbours.

name: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes
description:
**Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes** is a large administrative region in east-central France that stretches from the volcanic hills of the Auvergne across to the Alps, and as such it takes in several distinct wine areas rather than being a single appellation.

**Wines & grapes** — Within its borders lie parts of the northern and southern Rhône (Syrah reds, Viognier and other whites), the Gamay reds of Beaujolais, the alpine whites and reds of Savoie and Bugey, and the smaller vineyards of the Auvergne.

**Character** — Because it spans so much ground, the styles vary enormously, from powerful Rhône reds to featherlight mountain wines. What unites them is a French emphasis on place, with each sub-region shaped by its own soils and climate.

name: Marmara
description:
**Marmara** is a wine region in northwestern Turkey, wrapped around the Sea of Marmara and reaching into Turkish Thrace toward the borders with Greece and Bulgaria.

**Wines & grapes** — It grows a mix of indigenous Turkish grapes, such as the red Papazkarası and Adakarası, alongside international varieties like Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay.

**Character** — Cooled by the surrounding seas, this is one of Turkey's more temperate wine zones, giving fresher, more European-styled wines than the country's hotter interior. It is a key hub for Turkey's modern wine industry, blending native heritage with familiar international styles.

name: Lake County, California
description:
**Lake County, California** sits in the hills north of Napa and Sonoma, ringed around Clear Lake in the interior of California's North Coast. It has grown from a quiet grape-growing area into a source of well-regarded, well-priced wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Sauvignon Blanc is a local calling card, joined by Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and other warm-climate reds. Sub-areas such as the Red Hills, with their volcanic soils, have become known for concentrated Cabernet.

**Character** — High elevation and big shifts between hot days and cool nights give the wines bright acidity and firm structure. Strong mountain sunlight ripens the reds fully, while the cool nights help the whites keep their zip.

**Good to know** — Much of the fruit was historically sold to producers elsewhere, so Lake County often offers strong value.

name: Šumadija and Western Serbia
description:
**Šumadija and Western Serbia** is one of Serbia's broad wine zones, covering the hilly heartland of central Serbia and the country's western uplands. It is among the more established grape-growing parts of the country.

**Wines & grapes** — Both reds and whites are made, mixing international varieties with local Balkan grapes that have long been grown here.

**Character** — A continental climate with warm summers and cool hillside sites shapes the wines, which range from everyday bottlings to more ambitious estate cuvées as Serbia's wine scene has revived.

name: Puerto Plata
description:
**Puerto Plata** is a coastal province in the north of the Dominican Republic, on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola. It is far better known for beaches and tourism than for winemaking, and only a small amount of wine is associated with the area.

**Wines & grapes** — Any production is on a modest, mostly local scale, and the tropical setting is not a traditional home for vineyards.

**Character** — The hot, humid tropical climate makes conventional grape-growing very difficult, so wine here is a niche curiosity rather than an established regional style.

name: Zadar
description:
**Zadar** is a city and coastal area in northern Dalmatia, on Croatia's Adriatic shoreline. It is part of Croatia's long Mediterranean wine tradition rather than a single tightly-defined appellation.

**Wines & grapes** — The area leans on indigenous Croatian coastal varieties, including local whites and Dalmatian reds, alongside some international grapes.

**Character** — A sunny Mediterranean climate, sea breezes and stony coastal soils give fresh whites and warm, sun-ripened reds, often made by small family growers.

name: Šumadija
description:
**Šumadija** is a historic wine district in the hilly center of Serbia, around towns such as Kragujevac and Topola. It has deep roots in Serbian viticulture and is one of the country's most recognizable wine names.

**Wines & grapes** — Both reds and whites are produced, blending international varieties with native Balkan grapes; the district has seen a wave of renewal from serious estates.

**Character** — Gentle wooded hills and a continental climate of warm summers and cold winters shape the wines. The region's rolling, forested landscape gives it its name, which means "woodland," and its cellars range from long-standing to newly ambitious.

name: Armagnac
description:
**Armagnac** is a region in Gascony, in the southwest of France, celebrated as the home of France's oldest brandy. It gives its name to a distinctive grape spirit distilled from local white wine.

**Wines & grapes** — The base wines are made from white grapes such as Ugni Blanc, Folle Blanche, Colombard and Baco, then distilled and aged in oak. The same area also turns out fresh, aromatic still whites under the wider Côtes de Gascogne name.

**Character** — Armagnac is traditionally distilled once in a column still, giving a richer, more rustic spirit than Cognac, and it gains complexity through long barrel ageing.

**Good to know** — Vintage-dated Armagnacs are prized, since the region keeps stocks from individual years for decades.

name: Niagara Escarpment
description:
**Niagara Escarpment** is a cool-climate wine area on the Niagara Peninsula of Ontario, Canada, near Lake Ontario. It is one of Canada's leading regions for both table wines and its famous sweet wines.

**Wines & grapes** — Riesling, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir do well in the cool conditions, and the region is renowned for icewine, most often from Vidal and Riesling grapes left to freeze on the vine.

**Character** — The limestone ridge of the escarpment and the moderating influence of the lake temper the climate, protecting vines and lengthening the growing season. Cold winters make the concentrated, honeyed icewines possible, while the long, cool autumn preserves crisp acidity in the dry wines.

**Good to know** — Icewine here is strictly regulated, with grapes harvested naturally frozen at low temperatures.

name: Cederberg
description:
**Cederberg** is a small, high-altitude wine area in the mountains north of Cape Town, in South Africa's Western Cape. It is home to some of the country's loftiest vineyards.

**Wines & grapes** — Growers here work with both whites and reds, including crisp Sauvignon Blanc, Chenin Blanc and Chardonnay alongside structured reds such as Cabernet Sauvignon and Shiraz.

**Character** — Vineyards planted high in the Cederberg range enjoy cold nights, clean air and big day-to-night temperature swings, which lock in freshness and bright acidity. The remote, rugged mountain setting and cool nights set these wines apart from South Africa's warmer coastal regions.

**Good to know** — Its elevation makes it one of the highest and most isolated wine districts in South Africa.

name: Cafayate
description:
**Cafayate** is a high-altitude wine town in the Calchaquí Valleys of Salta province, in the far northwest of Argentina. It is the best-known winemaking hub of Argentina's northern highlands.

**Wines & grapes** — Torrontés, Argentina's signature aromatic white, is the star here, giving floral, perfumed wines. Malbec and other reds also thrive, taking on deep color and concentration.

**Character** — Vineyards sit at extreme elevations, often well above other wine regions, with intense sunlight, cool nights and a dry desert climate. That combination gives whites vivid aromatics and freshness, and reds firm structure with bright fruit.

**Good to know** — Some of the world's highest commercial vineyards are found in this corner of Argentina.

name: Maipo Valley
description:
**Maipo Valley** lies just south of Santiago in central Chile and is often called the classic heartland of Chilean red wine. It is one of the country's oldest and most prestigious regions.

**Wines & grapes** — Cabernet Sauvignon is king here, producing some of Chile's most acclaimed reds, often blended with Merlot, Carmenère and Syrah. Warmer and cooler pockets within the valley suit a range of styles.

**Character** — A Mediterranean climate of warm, dry summers, with cooling influences from the Andes and nearby coast, ripens grapes fully while keeping freshness. Wines from the higher, foothill vineyards near the mountains are especially prized for their structure and elegant, minty edge.

**Good to know** — Many of Chile's landmark estates and flagship Cabernets are rooted in Maipo.

name: Riverland
description:
**Riverland** is a large, warm inland region along the Murray River in South Australia. It is one of the country's biggest sources of grapes by volume and a workhorse of the Australian wine industry.

**Wines & grapes** — A wide range of varieties is grown, including Chardonnay, Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon and other popular grapes, much of it going into approachable, everyday wines and blends.

**Character** — The hot, dry climate and reliance on irrigation from the river favor ripe, generous, fruit-forward styles. While long associated with high-volume, value wines, the region has also seen growers experiment with hardy, warm-climate varieties suited to its sunshine.

**Good to know** — Riverland produces a very large share of Australia's total wine grape crush.

name: Manchuela
description:
**Manchuela** is a wine region in central-eastern Spain, in the Castilla-La Mancha area between the Júcar and Cabriel rivers. It has earned a reputation for characterful reds from a local grape.

**Wines & grapes** — Bobal is the signature variety, giving deeply colored, fresh reds, often alongside Tempranillo, Garnacha and international grapes; some crisp whites and rosés are made too.

**Character** — A high plateau setting with hot days, cool nights and limestone-rich soils helps the wines keep acidity and balance despite the warm climate. Modern producers have shown that old Bobal vines can yield lively, food-friendly reds rather than just bulk wine.

**Good to know** — The region's elevation sets it apart from the flatter, hotter plains nearby.

name: Waipara
description:
**Waipara** is a wine district in North Canterbury, on New Zealand's South Island, tucked into a river valley about an hour north of Christchurch.

**Wines & grapes** — Aromatic whites lead the way, especially Riesling and Pinot Gris, alongside Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc, while Pinot Noir is the standout red.

**Character** — The valley is sheltered from cool coastal winds by a range of hills, giving warm, dry days and long autumns that let fruit ripen slowly. Pockets of limestone in the soil are prized for lending finesse and mineral bite, particularly to the Rieslings and Pinot Noirs, which tend toward bright acidity and clear varietal definition.

name: Fleurieu Peninsula
description:
**Fleurieu Peninsula** is a broad wine zone in South Australia, stretching south of Adelaide toward the coast and taking in several well-known districts.

**Wines & grapes** — It is best known for full-bodied reds, above all Shiraz and Grenache, with Cabernet Sauvignon also widely planted; McLaren Vale and Langhorne Creek sit within its bounds.

**Character** — Proximity to the sea brings cooling maritime breezes that temper the warm Mediterranean-style climate, helping the reds keep freshness alongside their generous ripe fruit. Expect wines that are plush and warm-hearted, with the softly structured, berry-rich profile that has made this corner of South Australia a reliable source of characterful reds.

name: Anjou
description:
**Anjou** is a large wine district in the middle Loire Valley of western France, centred on the historic city of Angers.

**Wines & grapes** — It makes wines in every colour: dry and sweet whites from Chenin Blanc, reds from Cabernet Franc, and a famous range of rosés, including the off-dry Rosé d'Anjou and the pinker, fuller Cabernet d'Anjou.

**Character** — Soils shift from dark schist and slate in the west to softer limestone and sandstone in the east, a divide that shapes the wines' weight and mineral feel. The cool, temperate climate gives Chenin its trademark bracing acidity, which underpins everything from crisp dry whites to honeyed dessert wines built to age.

**Good to know** — Chenin Blanc's high acidity is what lets Anjou's sweet whites last for decades.

name: Matakana
description:
**Matakana** is a small, boutique wine district in New Zealand, set among rolling countryside north of Auckland on the North Island.

**Wines & grapes** — Being warm, it favours reds such as Merlot, Cabernet and Syrah, along with Pinot Gris and other whites from its scattered small estates.

**Character** — The climate is warm and humid with a strong maritime influence, and growers contend with autumn rain, which keeps yields modest and vineyards on the lookout for the right ripening years. Production is limited and artisanal, so the wines are largely enjoyed locally and rarely seen far from home.

name: Tikveš
description:
**Tikveš** is the largest and best-known wine region of North Macedonia, spread across the Vardar River valley in the centre of the country.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds dominate, led by the native Vranec, a deeply coloured grape, alongside Kratošija; whites include Smederevka and the aromatic Temjanika.

**Character** — The region enjoys a warm blend of continental and Mediterranean influences, with plenty of sunshine that ripens grapes fully and gives the reds their dark colour, ripe berry fruit and full body. It is a long-established wine-growing area with a substantial share of the nation's vineyards and a tradition of hearty, generous reds.

name: Cappadocia
description:
**Cappadocia** is a high-altitude wine area in central Anatolia, Turkey, famous more widely for its dramatic volcanic rock landscape and cave dwellings.

**Wines & grapes** — Local grapes are the mainstay, especially the white Emir, native to the area, along with reds such as Öküzgözü, Boğazkere and Kalecik Karası drawn from Anatolia's grape heritage.

**Character** — Vineyards sit on porous volcanic soils at considerable elevation, where hot days and cold nights on the Anatolian plateau help grapes hold acidity and freshness. The whites from Emir tend to be crisp and mineral, a reflection of the tuff-rich ground and the region's dry continental climate.

name: Cariñena DOP
description:
**Cariñena DOP** is a Spanish wine appellation in the Aragón region, in the northeast, taking its name from the town of Cariñena south of Zaragoza.

**Wines & grapes** — Reds are the heart of the region, built above all on old-vine Garnacha (Grenache), with the Cariñena grape (also called Mazuelo) and international varieties in support; some whites and rosés are also made.

**Character** — The climate is warm and dry with a strong continental swing between hot days and cool nights, and the cold Cierzo wind sweeps through the vineyards. On stony, poor soils the old vines yield concentrated, warming reds with ripe dark fruit.

**Good to know** — The town lends its name to the Cariñena grape, though the region today plants far more Garnacha.

name: Calatayud
description:
**Calatayud** is a wine appellation in the Aragón region of northeast Spain, in the hills of Zaragoza province.

**Wines & grapes** — It is celebrated for reds from old-vine Garnacha (Grenache), often grown on gnarled, low-yielding bush vines, with other varieties playing a supporting role.

**Character** — Vineyards climb to notable altitude on rugged, stony slopes where slate and other poor soils force the vines to struggle, concentrating flavour. Warm days and cool nights preserve freshness, giving reds that combine ripe, dark-berried fruit with a lifted, energetic feel and good structure from the aged vines.

name: Yecla
description:
**Yecla** is a compact wine appellation in the Murcia region of southeastern Spain, centred on the town of the same name.

**Wines & grapes** — Robust reds define it, built chiefly on Monastrell (the grape known elsewhere as Mourvèdre), which thrives in the heat, alongside Garnacha and other varieties.

**Character** — The climate is hot and dry with a semi-continental character, and the sun-baked conditions ripen Monastrell to give deeply coloured, full-bodied reds with ripe dark fruit and firm structure. Modest rainfall and stony soils keep yields low and flavours concentrated in this warm inland corner of Spain.

name: Bergerac
description:
**Bergerac** is a wine district in southwest France, sitting along the Dordogne River just east of the Bordeaux region.

**Wines & grapes** — It shares Bordeaux's grape palette, making reds from Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc, and whites both dry and sweet from Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadelle; the sweet-wine enclave of Monbazillac lies within its orbit.

**Character** — The temperate, gently maritime-influenced climate produces reds that are typically softer and lighter than their Bordeaux neighbours, with fresh red-fruit character and approachable structure. Its long history and Bordeaux-like styles make it a friendly, well-priced source of classic southwest French wine.

**Good to know** — Bergerac often offers Bordeaux-style wines at gentler prices.

name: Malokarpatská
description:
**Malokarpatská** is a wine region in Slovakia, running along the Small Carpathian hills northeast of Bratislava.

**Wines & grapes** — Whites are the strength, including Grüner Veltliner, Welschriesling and Riesling, while reds such as Frankovka modrá (Blaufränkisch) are also grown.

**Character** — The wooded slopes give sheltered, sun-facing vineyard sites in a cool continental climate, favouring fresh, aromatic whites with lively acidity. It is one of the country's most historic wine-growing areas, with a long tradition centred on towns like Pezinok and Modra.

name: Carnuntum
description:
**Carnuntum** is a wine region in Lower Austria, lying east of Vienna between the capital and the Slovak border.

**Wines & grapes** — It has a strong reputation for reds, above all Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch, while whites such as Grüner Veltliner and Chardonnay are also made.

**Character** — The warm Pannonian climate, with hot summers moderated by the Danube to the north, ripens the red grapes fully, giving wines that are supple and fruit-forward yet retain freshness. On varied soils of gravel, loess and loam, growers craft characterful reds that have raised the region's profile in recent decades.

name: Okanagan Valley
description:
**Okanagan Valley** is the leading wine region of British Columbia, Canada, stretching along a chain of long lakes in the province's dry interior. It has become the country's best-known source of serious wine outside Ontario.

**Wines & grapes** — Both colours are made across a wide palette. The cooler north favours aromatic whites such as Riesling, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay and Gewürztraminer, while the warmer, near-desert south ripens Bordeaux reds like Merlot and Cabernet, along with Syrah and Pinot Noir. Icewine is a specialty in colder vintages.

**Character** — The valley's length gives it a striking range of climates, from cool lakeside sites to sun-baked benches near the US border. Warm days, cool nights and low rainfall produce wines with bright acidity and clear varietal definition.

**Good to know** — The moderating effect of the lakes helps vines survive the sharp continental winters.

name: Nova Scotia
description:
**Nova Scotia** is a cool-climate wine region on Canada's Atlantic coast, with much of its vineyard concentrated in the sheltered Annapolis Valley and around the Bay of Fundy.

**Wines & grapes** — The signature is crisp, high-acid white and sparkling wine. Growers rely heavily on cold-hardy hybrids such as L'Acadie Blanc, Seyval Blanc and Vidal, alongside aromatic vinifera like Riesling. The province has its own appellation-style white blend, Tidal Bay, designed to express the maritime climate.

**Character** — Cold winters, a short growing season and a strong ocean influence give the wines lean bodies, zesty acidity and low alcohol. These conditions suit traditional-method sparkling wine particularly well.

**Good to know** — It is one of the coolest and most northerly wine regions in North America.

name: Wachau
description:
**Wachau** is a small, prestigious white-wine region in Austria, set along a dramatic stretch of the Danube west of Vienna. Its steep terraced vineyards are among the most celebrated in Central Europe.

**Wines & grapes** — It is almost entirely devoted to dry white wine from two grapes: Grüner Veltliner and Riesling. The region uses its own ripeness classification, from the light Steinfeder through Federspiel to the concentrated, powerful Smaragd.

**Character** — Rocky terraced slopes, poor primary-rock soils and a meeting of warm Pannonian and cool northern air give the wines great precision, minerality and length. Grüner shows peppery, citrus notes; Riesling turns stony and stone-fruited.

**Good to know** — Many of the terraces are dry-stone walled and worked entirely by hand.

name: Murrumbateman
description:
**Murrumbateman** is a small wine district in New South Wales, Australia, sitting within the broader Canberra District wine region north of the national capital.

**Wines & grapes** — It is best known for cool-climate reds and aromatic whites, with Shiraz and Riesling as the standout varieties. Co-fermented Shiraz-Viognier is something of a local calling card, and Chardonnay and other varieties are also grown.

**Character** — Although it lies well inland, high elevation brings cool nights and a genuine continental climate, giving reds fragrant, peppery spice and firm structure, and whites bright, taut acidity.

**Good to know** — The district punches above its size and helped establish Canberra's reputation for elegant, spicy Shiraz.

name: Villány
description:
**Villány** is Hungary's most famous red-wine region, lying in the warm far south of the country near the Croatian border. It has a long winemaking history and a reputation for full-bodied, structured reds.

**Wines & grapes** — The focus is firmly on red wine. Bordeaux varieties such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Merlot do well, alongside local grapes including Kékfrankos (Blaufränkisch) and Portugieser. Cabernet Franc, sometimes labelled Villányi Franc, is a particular local strength.

**Character** — One of Hungary's warmest and sunniest areas, with limestone and loess soils, it ripens grapes fully to give deep, ripe, tannic reds often matured in oak.

**Good to know** — It sits at the southern end of Hungary and is known for its lively wine-village culture.
